info.name: Brgy-RBIM API
info.description:
Barangay RBIM API collection. Base URL: http://localhost:8000.

## Auth flow (Sanctum stateful / cookie-session)

This API uses Sanctum in **stateful (SPA) mode** — there are no Bearer tokens. Authentication is entirely cookie-based:

1. **GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie** — seeds the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. Must run first.
2. **POST /api/v1/auth/login** — Laravel calls `Auth::login()` and `$request->session()->regenerate()`. On success, the server sets a `laravel_session` cookie. Postman's cookie jar stores it automatically.
3. All subsequent requests are authenticated by the `laravel_session` cookie sent automatically by the cookie jar. No manual token handling needed.

### CSRF header on mutating requests
Every POST and PATCH request must include the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header. Postman reads the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie value and sends it as a header automatically **if you enable "Automatically follow redirects" and "Send cookies" in Postman settings**, or you can copy the cookie value into the `xsrf_token` collection variable and let the pre-set header send it.

> **Tip:** In Postman Desktop, go to **Settings → General** and make sure **"Automatically follow redirects"** and **"Send cookies"** are both on. The cookie jar will then handle the session cookie and XSRF token transparently.

variable.description: Value of the XSRF-TOKEN cookie set by GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie. Copy it here if Postman does not forward it automatically via the cookie jar. Used in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on all POST and PATCH requests.
ID of the target user for /users/{user} routes.
ID of the target user-role record for /user-roles/{userRole}/status.

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
Endpoints for CSRF seeding, login/logout, current-user info, audit logs, and password management.

**Request order matters:** run Get CSRF Cookie first, then Login. The session cookie set by Login is carried automatically by Postman's cookie jar for all subsequent requests.

request.description:
**Run this first, before Login.**

Tells Sanctum to issue the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. Postman's cookie jar stores it automatically. The value is then forwarded as the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on every subsequent POST/PATCH via the `{{xsrf_token}}` variable (or automatically by the cookie jar if Postman's cookie forwarding is enabled).

No request body. No session required.

header.description: Value of the XSRF-TOKEN cookie set by Get CSRF Cookie. Required by Sanctum's CSRF middleware on all POST requests.

request.description:
**Run after Get CSRF Cookie.**

Authenticates the user via `Auth::login()` and `$request->session()->regenerate()`. On success, the server sets a `laravel_session` cookie — Postman's cookie jar picks it up automatically and sends it with every subsequent request. No token is returned.

**Rules (LoginRequest):**
- `username` — required, string, max 45 characters
- `password` — required, string

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all POST requests.

request.description: Invalidates the current session. Requires an active `laravel_session` cookie (sent automatically by the cookie jar). No request body needed.
Returns the currently authenticated user's profile. Session cookie is sent automatically by the cookie jar. No request body needed.
Returns the audit/activity logs for the currently authenticated user. Session cookie is sent automatically by the cookie jar. No request body needed.

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all POST requests.

request.description:
Changes the authenticated user's own password. Session cookie is sent automatically by the cookie jar.

**Rules (ChangePasswordRequest):**
- `current_password` — required, string
- `new_password` — required, string, must be confirmed
- `new_password_confirmation` — must match `new_password` (Laravel `confirmed` rule)

item.name: User Management
item.description: Endpoints for listing, creating, and inspecting users, updating their status, resetting passwords, and managing role assignments. All endpoints require an active session — the `laravel_session` cookie is sent automatically by Postman's cookie jar after a successful Login.

request.description: Returns a list of all users. Session cookie sent automatically. No request body needed.

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all POST requests.

request.description:
Creates a new user account and links it to an existing barangay personnel record.

**Rules (StoreUserRequest):**
- `username` — required, string, max 45, unique in `user.username`
- `personnel_id` — required, integer, must exist in `barangay_personnel.personnel_id`, unique in `user.personnel_id` (one account per personnel)
- `role_id` — required, integer, must exist in `role.role_id`
Returns a single user by their ID. Set the `user_id` collection variable to the target user's ID. Session cookie sent automatically. No request body needed.

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all PATCH requests.

request.description:
Updates the status of a user account.

**Rules (UpdateUserStatusRequest):**
- `user_status_id` — required, integer, must exist in `user_status.user_status_id`

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all POST requests.

request.description: Resets the target user's password to a system-generated default. No request body — the controller uses no Form Request for this action. Session cookie sent automatically.
Returns all roles assigned to the target user. Session cookie sent automatically. No request body needed.

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all POST requests.

request.description:
Assigns an additional role to the target user.

**Rules (StoreUserRoleRequest):**
- `role_id` — required, integer, must exist in `role.role_id`, must not already be assigned to this user (unique per user in `user_role`)

header.description: CSRF token required by Sanctum on all PATCH requests.

request.description:
Enables or disables a specific user-role assignment.

**Rules (UpdateUserRoleStatusRequest):**
- `enable` — required, boolean (`true` to enable, `false` to disable)

Set the `user_role_id` collection variable to the target `user_role` record ID.
